comparison: Both evaluations support the RNAseq findings (C5, C6, C19-C21). OpenEval emphasizes the technical quality of PCA and differential expression analysis with appropriate experimental design. Peer reviewers acknowledge the approach as providing valuable insight into second-order gustatory neurons without raising concerns about the core transcriptomic findings.

Both evaluations support the GO analysis and differential expression findings (C23-C25). OpenEval notes these are inferential interpretations rather than direct functional demonstrations. Peer reviewers accept the differential expression findings and describe the approach as elegant without questioning the GO analysis interpretations.

Both evaluations support the neurotransmitter receptor and biosynthetic enzyme expression data (C30, C32-C34). OpenEval highlights consistency with prior literature and clear documentation of metabolic state effects. Peer reviewers treat these as descriptive molecular characterization results without challenge.

Both evaluations support the neuropeptide and receptor expression findings (C35-C37). OpenEval notes functional interpretations are speculative inferences from expression data. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these broader molecular characterization findings as valuable data for future studies.

Both evaluations strongly support the Leucokinin upregulation findings (C41-C44, C53-C58). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of three independent methods (RNAseq, qPCR, immunohistochemistry). All peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this finding with Reviewer 1 confirming higher expression when starved and Reviewer 2 noting support from multiple techniques.

Both evaluations address connectivity claims (C59-C67) but with different emphases. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, highlighting exceptional convergence from four independent methods (trans-Tango, GRASP, active-GRASP, BacTrace). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging strong connectivity evidence but expressing concerns about methodological discrepancies and lack of physiological support for modulation.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about connectomic analysis (C68-C79). OpenEval emphasizes significant limitations with incomplete connectome annotation (far fewer GRNs identified than expected). Peer Reviewer 2 questions whether the connectomic section is out of place and unclear in its utility, though acknowledges the data.

Both evaluations address PER behavioral experiments (C81, C84-C89) but differ in assessment. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate experimental design and statistical analysis, noting the tsh-Gal80 control shows no effect. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the phenotype can be clearly assigned to SELK neurons specifically and noting the behavioral section lacks depth.

Both evaluations support the flyPAD findings (C90-C92, C94). OpenEval notes the negative result (no effect on sustained feeding) contrasts with PER results and is appropriately acknowledged. Peer reviewers accept the distinction between feeding initiation and sustained feeding without challenge, though note overall behavioral section lacks depth.

OpenEval supports the quantification of trans-Tango labeled neurons (C17) as a straightforward observation with adequate sample sizes. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific claim.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the speculative explanation for discrepancies in trans-Tango sensitivity (C100-C101), noting it remains untested but is appropriately presented as speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation directly addresses this methodological limitation.

OpenEval supports the documentation of technical limitations preventing functional imaging (C108-C109). Peer Reviewer 3 mentions this limitation in passing but no dedicated peer review evaluation addresses these specific claims.

Peer reviewers support the overall conclusions and novelty of the study (C95-C99), with the editor stating evidence is convincing and reviewers acknowledging the novel model and valuable insights. OpenEval addresses some of these claims (C95, C97, C98) within other result groupings but has no dedicated evaluation of the overall conclusions as a set.
